children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery refers to the sensing and relay of force, vibration, and tissue resistance from surgical instruments back to the operating surgeon.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal uses patient-specific imaging and computational models to let a surgical team practice a planned procedure before entering the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers technologies that reduce or cancel physiological hand tremor during delicate procedures such as retinal, vascular, and neurosurgery.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery is the practice of performing surgical procedures on a patient from a distance using robotic instruments, telecommunication links, and real-time imaging.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation is the use of machines and software to help plan, guide, and perform operations. AI in this field now does concrete tasks like outlining a tumor from a scan, adjusting a robotic arm's movement to cancel a surgeon's hand tremor, and simulating a procedure before the real one. It is not autonomous surgery. The surgeon remains in control, and the AI works as a tool for measurement, prediction, and motion filtering. Current systems also relay force information back to the surgeon's hands through haptic feedback, and some experimental setups allow an operation to be performed from a distant console. These are working systems in operating rooms and research labs, not just proposals.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Resection planning and margin analysis can now mark likely tumor boundaries in images, but the final call still belongs to a pathologist or surgeon, and the software can miss irregular or rare cases. Haptic feedback is good enough to feel resistance in training simulators, but reproducing the full texture and tension of living tissue remains unsolved. Virtual surgical rehearsal works for anatomy that is stable and well imaged, yet it struggles with soft tissue that shifts during an operation. Tremor stabilisation is the most mature piece, with active filtering already used in microsurgery, though it cannot restore a surgeon's natural touch. Remote telesurgery has been demonstrated over short and long distances, but it depends on network speed and reliability, and any delay can make fine work unsafe. The honest limit is that these tools reduce some errors and improve planning, but they do not remove the need for human judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to understand how a tumor is outlined before cutting should start with Resection Planning and Margins, which covers the imaging and boundary work. From there, Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery explains what the surgeon feels through the instruments and why that sense matters. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal sits next to those two, because it uses the planned margins and the feel of the tools to let a surgeon practice a specific patient's anatomy. Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery is the page for the motion side, showing how small unwanted movements are filtered out during delicate work. Remote Telesurgery connects all of these across distance, since it relies on stable planning, reliable feedback, rehearsal, and motion control to operate through a console. Together the pages move from planning, to touch, to practice, to motion, and finally to distance.
